note: Dev set of the team-arms comparison (B4), 40 cases, written 2026-11-24 by an independent case-author session that read CASES.md, cases.py, the schema, the quick example (shape only), teamspace/fixtures.py and dclab_core/target_contract.py, and never the arms' code, prompts, scorer or runner. Each expected end is what a careful human team would reach from the invented fixtures; numbers in scripts are said by the scripted people.

cases.title: Rank accounts by risk of failing to renew, plainly worded
cases.opening: Can our data rank accounts by the risk of failing to renew by the contractual renewal date, seven days before each renewal?

replies.text: Yes: failure to renew by the contractual renewal date.

must_understand: The outcome is failure to renew by the contractual date, already stated
The prediction moment is seven days before each renewal
renewed_by_date is the outcome, never an input
acceptable_approaches: Check the sample's columns, dates and label, then report feasibility
forbidden: Ask what churn means when the person already said it
Claim a model was trained or accounts were scored

cases.notes: Plain control: rules should pass. No question is needed; a backup reply exists in case one is asked.

cases.title: Explicit cancellation risk on the table with the CRM log
cases.opening: Seven days before each renewal, can we rank accounts by the chance they explicitly cancel? The CRM cancellation log is attached to the table.

replies.text: Explicit cancellation: the customer tells us they are cancelling.

must_understand: The outcome is an explicit cancellation, recorded in cancelled_at
cancellation_reason is written only after a cancellation and must not be an input

cases.title: Order 1042: arrival time and first-offer acceptance
cases.opening: Order 1042 was dispatched at 18:00. What is its estimated arrival time, and how likely is a courier to accept the first offer?

must_understand: Two separate questions: arrival time (ETA specialist) and first-offer acceptance (acceptance specialist)
Both answers are simulated fixtures, not measured models

cases.title: Sales capacity asked directly
cases.opening: How many renewal calls can your team make in the week before renewal?

replies.text: Failure to renew by the contractual renewal date.
We can make 23 calls that week.
Accounts renewing in the next 60 days that agreed to be contacted.

must_understand: Sales asks its own team for its call capacity and returns the member's number

cases.title: Customers who quietly drift off at contract end
cases.opening: Which customers quietly drift off when their contract comes up? I'd like to know a week before it does.

replies.text: I mean they don't renew by the contract's renewal date.

must_understand: 'Quietly drift off when the contract comes up' means not renewing by the renewal date, not an explicit cancellation
A week before renewal is the prediction moment
acceptable_approaches: Read the wording as non-renewal without a needless question

cases.notes: Free wording; a careful team reads it as non-renewal. If a team asks anyway, the backup reply keeps the case moving (the question counts as needless only).

cases.title: Who is slipping away before their contract ends
cases.opening: Who's slipping away before their contract ends? I want a heads-up 7 days before renewal.

replies.text: I mean they don't renew when the contract comes up for renewal.

must_understand: 'Slipping away before the contract ends' could mean an early cancellation or a non-renewal: one question settles it
After the answer, the outcome is non-renewal by the renewal date

cases.notes: Genuinely ambiguous wording, so one question is needed.

cases.title: Order 1042 in casual words
cases.opening: Order 1042 left the kitchen at 6pm. When's it landing at the customer's door, and will a rider grab it on the first ping?

must_understand: 'When is it landing' is the arrival estimate; 'grab it on the first ping' is first-offer acceptance
Both figures are simulated

cases.title: Who should my reps ring before subscriptions run out
cases.opening: Which accounts should my reps ring before they let their subscription run out? We'd call seven days before renewal, and only accounts renewing in the next 60 days.

replies.text: Not renewing by the renewal date is what I mean.
22 calls is what we can manage.
Accounts renewing in the next 60 days that agreed to be contacted.

must_understand: 'Let their subscription run out' is non-renewal
Sales must give its capacity; Marketing is not asked (no offer requested)

cases.title: Person means cancellation; table holds only renewals
cases.opening: Seven days before renewal, rank accounts by how likely they are to cancel.

replies.text: I mean an explicit cancellation: the customer tells us they are cancelling.

must_understand: The person means explicit cancellation
renewal_v1 records only failure to renew; it has no cancellation record
The CRM cancellation log comes from Business
forbidden: Rank by non-renewal and call it cancellation risk

cases.notes: Next owner: the Business team, which holds the record that is missing (contracts system or CRM). Sara belongs to Business, but the expected owner is the team 'business', not 'home' or 'person'.

cases.title: Customers are leaving: cancellation log available
cases.opening: Customers are leaving us. Seven days before renewal, which accounts are most at risk?

replies.text: Explicit cancellations only: the ones who actually tell us they are cancelling.

must_understand: 'Leaving' is ambiguous: ask once
After the answer the outcome is explicit cancellation, recorded in cancelled_at

cases.title: Turning off auto-renew

cases.opening: Seven days before renewal, which accounts will we lose?

must_understand: 'Lose' could be cancellation or non-renewal; the team must ask and wait

cases.title: Kitchen adds 8 minutes after the dispatch brief
cases.opening: For order 1042, dispatched at 18:00: when will it arrive, and how likely is the first courier offer to be accepted?

must_understand: The kitchen delay moves the arrival by the same 8 minutes
The acceptance estimate is not rerun
judge_key.adaptation_check: After the delay, the current brief shows 18:40 and links to the superseded estimate.

cases.title: Kitchen delay added then withdrawn
cases.opening: What time will order 1042 reach the customer? It was dispatched at 18:00.

must_understand: Only the arrival estimate is asked
A withdrawn delay (0) restores the original arrival
judge_key.adaptation_check: After +8 the arrival is 18:40; after the delay is withdrawn it is 18:32 again.

cases.title: Outcome corrected from non-renewal to cancellation
cases.opening: Seven days before each renewal, can we rank accounts by risk of failing to renew by the contractual renewal date?

replies.text: Failure to renew by the contractual renewal date.
Correction: only explicit cancellations count, not lapses.

must_understand: The first answer (non-renewal) is feasible
After the correction the outcome is explicit cancellation, which this table does not record
Business supplies the cancellation log
judge_key.adaptation_check: The revised report is blocked and names the missing cancellation record.

cases.notes: Next owner: the Business team, which holds the record that is missing (contracts system or CRM). Sara belongs to Business, but the expected owner is the team 'business', not 'home' or 'person'.

cases.title: Outcome corrected from cancellation to non-renewal
cases.opening: Seven days before renewal, which accounts are likely to explicitly cancel? The table has the CRM cancellation log.

replies.text: Explicit cancellation: the customer tells us they are cancelling.
We've changed our minds: the outcome is failure to renew by the contractual renewal date.

must_understand: Both outcomes are recorded in this table
After the correction the outcome is renewed_by_date
judge_key.adaptation_check: The revised report rests on non-renewal, not cancellation.
